summary:
Earth Analogs for Moon and Mars Bases is an educational visual guide and presentation designed to show how extreme environments on Earth help NASA prepare for future human space exploration.

Building permanent bases on the Moon and Mars is expensive and dangerous, so scientists test rovers, spacesuits, and survival technologies right here on Earth first. This project compares four key terrestrial analogs with their space counterparts: the Atacama Desert (Mars), Hawaiian Lava Tubes (Moon shelters), McMurdo Dry Valleys in Antarctica (Lunar South Pole water ice), and Iceland’s volcanic fields (astronaut field training).

By connecting real NASA mission imagery with clear explanations, this project makes space science accessible and demonstrates how studying our own planet unlocks safe human life beyond Earth.
details: This project presents a side by side visual comparison between extreme environments on Earth and targeted landing or base sites on the Moon and Mars.
